summary: Hyrtacus (Ancient Greek: Ὕρτακος) is a Trojan-War figure, comrade of Priam, who married Arisbe daughter of Merops of Percote after Priam set her aside for Hecuba. By her he fathered Asius (atlas asius-hyrtacid), the Hellespontine ally who fights at Troy. Virgil later credits him with sons Nisus and Hippocoon.
etymology: Ancient Greek Ὕρτακος; the name is sometimes linked to the Cretan town Hyrtacus / Hyrtacina.

sections.heading: Father of Asius
paragraphs: Homer names Hyrtacus chiefly as the patronym of Asius, who leads men from Arisbe, Percote, Practius, Sestus, and Abydus. Apollodorus synchronizes the house with Priam's early marriage to Arisbe: after that divorce Hyrtacus takes her, and Asius is their son.
In the Aeneid Hyrtacus is also father of Nisus (and of an archery-contest Hippocoon). His own parentage is not given in the surviving Greek catalogues.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id hyrtacus-trojan is the Trojan comrade and father of Asius alone — not to be merged with later Latin namesakes or with the Cretan toponym.
